content.rendered:
Is this not the fast that I have chosen: to loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? God’s chosen fast is not empty religion. It is authority in action.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, August 1, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Is this not the fast that I have chosen: To loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke?”
Isaiah 58:6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Isaiah 58 records one of the most stunning corrections in the entire Old Testament. Israel had been fasting. They had been performing all the religious motions. And they were complaining to God that He did not seem to be answering. Isaiah delivers the Lord’s response. Your fasting has been a religious performance. The kind of fast I have chosen looks different. It looses bonds. It undoes heavy burdens. It sets the oppressed free. It breaks every yoke.

The Passion Translation renders the verse with striking power: “No, this is the kind of fast day I’m after: to break the chains of injustice, get rid of exploitation in the workplace, free the oppressed, cancel debts” (Isaiah 58:6 MSG). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Is not this the fast that I have chosen: to loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the bands of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every [enslaving] yoke?” (Isaiah 58:6 AMPC).

The fast God chooses is not weight loss. It is not a religious exercise the fasting person can boast about. It is the alignment of the fasting believer with the God who breaks yokes off human lives. When the believer fasts, denying the flesh and turning their appetite toward the Father, they are agreeing with the Kingdom priority of freeing the captive. The fast becomes a weapon in the believer’s authority arsenal, because it is a fast agreeing with what the Lord has already declared over every yoke on every human life.

The New Testament echoes this. Jesus said in Mark 9:29 that certain spiritual battles yield only through prayer and fasting. Paul recorded his own fasting in 2 Corinthians 11. The early church fasted before major decisions in Acts 13. The pattern of the Bible is consistent. Fasting, when united with faith in the finished work of Christ, is not an attempt to earn something from God. It is agreement with God, and it breaks yokes.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the encouragement today is not to introduce a legalistic fasting regimen. It is to see fasting as a Kingdom weapon. When you fast, do it with a clear intention. Loose bonds. Undo burdens. Set the oppressed free. Break yokes. Yoke of addiction. Yoke of fear. Yoke of poverty. Yoke of generational bondage. The fast God chooses breaks them, because the fast God chooses agrees with what Jesus has already accomplished at the cross. Walk in that reality when the Spirit calls you into a fast.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that the fast You have chosen breaks every yoke. When You call me into fasting, I do not fast to earn from You. I fast to agree with You. I agree that every bond of wickedness must be loosed. Every heavy burden must be undone. Every yoke must be broken. What Jesus has already accomplished at the cross is what my fasting agrees with. I walk in the freedom of the fast that You have chosen, and every yoke over my life, my family, and my calling breaks in Jesus’ name. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The fast God has chosen breaks every yoke. When I fast in agreement with Him, bonds are loosed and burdens are undone. What Jesus accomplished at the cross, the fast enforces on earth.
